story.head: Unstoppable force vs. Immovable object
paras: The Sabres have won two in a row, while the Senators (8-5-1) lost 6-5 in overtime to Los Angeles on Thursday. This is an Atlantic Division matchup, with the Senators fifth (tied for tenth in the NHL) and the Sabres seventh (tied for 16th). The Atlantic has been the strongest of the four divisions so far.

The Senators’ record (.607) is running ahead of what their chances are worth (.531), largely thanks to pulling off wins in one-goal games. The Sabres’ record (.577) is about what their chances are worth.

The Senators (2nd) and the Sabres (3rd) both rarely get pinned in their own end. The Senators draw more penalties than they take (3rd) and play slow, tight games (3rd lowest). On the other side, the Sabres get their shots through better than almost anyone (2nd), but don't block many shots (30th). The Sabres’ good looks will be harder to come by against the Sens. On top of that, the Senators hit a lot, but the Sabres mostly don’t.

Tim Stützle (8 G / 11 A / 19 P in 14 GP) leads the Senators in scoring and is tied for tenth in the NHL, with seven points in his last five games. Drake Batherson (8 G / 8 A / 16 P in 14 GP) is next in line, with ten points in his last five games. For the Sabres, Tage Thompson (8 G / 7 A / 15 P in 13 GP) leads the way in scoring, with seven points in his last five games and eight goals in eleven games against Ottawa since 2023-24. Jack Quinn (7 G / 5 A / 12 P in 13 GP) isn’t far behind.

Jonas Johansson (1-1-0 / .859 SV% in 3 GS) will likely start for Ottawa. Buffalo has two options in net: Ukko-Pekka Luukkonen (3-3-3 / .866 SV% in 8 GS) and Colten Ellis (3-1-0 / .880 SV% in 5 GS). Luukkonen has started six of their last ten games, but Ellis got the last one on Thursday. It’s anyone’s guess who gets the net.
